Subject: Post-demo: Dedicated reserved SKU questions + TPS / token mix details

Hi Elena — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and a set of concrete asks so we can size Dedicated capacity for DeepPrint: 

Recap (from the call)
- Primary workload: user-facing document summarization + multi-turn editing.
- Burst pattern: steady baseline ~120 rps during business hours with short bursts up to ~600 rps for 10–15 minute windows (marketing spikes).
- Model family: you evaluated an open LLM similar to MPT-30B and also mentioned a smaller low-latency variant for short edits.

What we need from you (please fill / attach):
1) Token profile CSV (prompt tokens avg, response tokens avg, 95th pct tokens) — rough numbers are fine. (attached: template)
2) Target p95 latency SLO for end-to-end response (e.g., 300ms / 500ms / 1s).
3) Any requirement for private networking (VPC) or air-gapped on-prem (or hosted/dedicated ok).
4) Retention / audit log length (for compliance) and whether keys will be customer-managed (KMS/HSM).

Preliminary questions from our side that will affect GPU recommendation:
- Is the 120 rps baseline per geographic region or global? If multi-region, which regions?
- Do you expect long (>2k token) prompts regularly (batching considerations)?

Next steps: if you can send the token CSV and confirm the p95 target I’ll send a Dedicated SKU estimate (GPU mix options) and an ops plan (autoscaling/burst). Karthik will also chime in on quantization/latency tradeoffs.

Thanks — Rachel

Thanks Elena — this is perfect and very helpful. Attached is an initial Dedicated SKU estimate (PDF) with three options and tradeoffs. Highlights in brief: 

Option A (cost‑sensitive): 6x A10G nodes (reserved) + autoscale burst pool
- Best for: cost-focused teams with tolerance for slightly higher p95 (~500–800ms for your model profile).
- Expected sustained throughput: ~200–300 rps at p95 ~700ms (with long-tail batching off).

Option B (balanced): 4x H100 (80GB) inference nodes + 8x L4 augment instances for low-latency edits
- Best for: strict p95 for interactive editor (<=600ms) while keeping cost predictable.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~400 rps p95 ~450–600ms; burst to 800 rps using reserved burst pool and temporary routing to hosted fallback if needed.

Option C (latency-first): 8x H100 + dedicated KV cache tier, pre-warming for hot prompts
- Best for: p95 <=350–450ms on typical requests and heavy long-context cases.
- Expected throughput: ~700+ rps at low latency; higher cost.

Key ops notes that affect sizing:
- Concurrency shaping: target a per-GPU active request concurrency of ~8–12 for H100 and ~6–10 for A10G given your token mix (avg total ~570 tokens).
- Batching: Redwood runtime can batch short requests aggressively; long-document requests should be routed to dedicated low-concurrency lanes to avoid head-of-line latency.
- KV/prefix caching: will substantially reduce token work for iterative editing flows; we recommend a small dedicated cache tier for Option B/C.
- VPC: we support VPC peering + customer KMS; we’ll surface a network diagram and peering checklist in the onboarding doc.

Next actionable items
1) Karthik — can you confirm the per-GPU concurrency recommendation for Option B with the given token profile and whether fp16 quantization yields meaningful latency drops for this model family?
2) Elena — confirm which option you want priced as a next step (A/B/C) and whether to include a 20% burst buffer in the reserved commit.
3) Rachel/Marcus — schedule a short ops call (30 min) with DeepPrint infra to walk the VPC peering and KMS steps. Proposed: Thu 7/1 or Fri 7/2 in the morning PST.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the PDF attached and a HubSpot update.

Rachel

Hi Elena / team — quick technical follow-up on Rachel's options. Inline: 

Per-GPU concurrency estimates (based on provided token profile: prompt_avg=420, response_avg=150, avg_total~570):
- H100 (80GB) inference nodes: 10–14 active requests/GPU to hit the Option B latency band (p95 ~450–600ms) when using mixed precision (fp16) and kernel-level optimizations.
- A10G: 6–9 active requests/GPU for similar throughput targets but expect p95 uplift of ~150–300ms vs H100 for long documents. Good for cheaper sustained throughput with higher p95.
- L4 (small instances): optimized for low-latency short edits — use as an augmentation for small requests (<=150 tokens total). Not ideal for long-context summarization.

Quantization/precision note: We can push int8 (with per-layer calibration) for cost-sensitive paths; however, for your long-document summarization, int8 may introduce small quality regressions. fp16 is the recommended baseline.

Routing recommendation:
- Route interactive editor traffic to a hybrid lane: L4 pool for under-150-token edits, H100 pool for everything else. Use autoscaler with a warm spare pool (5–10% reserved GPUs) to handle 10–15 minute bursts.

If DeepPrint confirms Option B, I’ll prepare a simple performance-runbook and suggested concurrency limits per GPU node for the onboarding docs.

–Karthik
